attempted_claim: Let T_{3,inf} be the countable biregular tree whose bipartition classes have valences 3 and countably infinite respectively, with vertex set N, and let G=Aut(T_{3,inf}) with the pointwise-convergence Polish topology (a non-locally-compact non-archimedean Polish group) acting continuously on X=G by conjugation g.x=gxg^{-1}. Is the conjugacy relation E_G^X essentially countable, i.e. Borel reducible to a countable Borel equivalence relation? A complete answer is either an explicit Borel reduction to a countable Borel equivalence relation with correctness proof, or a proof that some invariant dense G_delta X_0 is generically ergodic against every countable Borel equivalence relation with meagre classes, witnessing that no such reduction exists.
decisive_failure: Both horns of the target remain open: the YES horn lacks a Borel countable coding of elliptic elements with infinite fixed subtrees and infinite-order branch permutations, and the NO horn lacks a verified turbulent or generically ergodic invariant dense G_delta with meagre classes; finite-truncation probes cannot resolve infinite-valence behaviour and no original emergent increment survived review.
